title: Continuous standby certification with traffic-shadowing and rollback safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an automated, continuously-running certification pipeline that keeps warm-standby regions and model-variant fallbacks in a verifiable ready state. Certification combines passive health probes, traffic-shadowing with synthetic load, and a rollback-safe automated switchover mechanism. The goal is to reduce mean time to failover and eliminate manual priming steps during incidents.

Motivation and goals:
- Customers must tolerate regional failover without significant degradation in latency or unit cost. Warm standbys should be ready to accept production traffic within defined SLOs (cold-start < 250ms additional latency, model-initialization < 30s).
- Current manual priming is error-prone and drifts over time. We need automated continuous verification and a safe, auditable switchover path for policy-based routing changes (region selection + tier routing + fallback model variants).

Scope and what success looks like (Acceptance criteria):
1) Continuous certification service runs every 10 minutes per standby region: performs health checks, KV-cache warming probes, and model-variant inference smoke tests using replayed production prompts.
2) Traffic-shadowing harness mirrors 1% of sampled production requests to standby model variant with no impact on user metrics; results sent to a quality dashboard and drift-alerting rules.
3) Automated readiness score computed per-standby (0-100). Score >= 85 required for automatic region failover.
4) Orchestrated switchover flow: decision engine triggers canary traffic shift to standby (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback if error rate or latency exceeds thresholds.
5) Audit trail: every certification run and switchover decision stored in the Console timeline and linked to the incident/rollout.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Passive probes vs. synthetic traffic: passive probes are low-cost but miss KV-warm paths. We use hybrid approach: frequent lightweight probes + scheduled synthetic shadowing bursts for deeper validation.
- Shadowing overhead: 1% mirror rate chosen to limit cost while providing representative samples; configurable per-customer. Higher mirror rates increase confidence but raise unit cost and potential side-effects (telemetry volume).
- Readiness scoring: combine binary health checks (container status, gRPC liveness), end-to-end p50/p95 latency deltas, and model output similarity metrics (embedding cosine + tokens divergence). Avoid single-metric gating to reduce noisy flips.
- Rollback policy: conservative automatic rollback on early anomalies during canary ramp. Full automated cutover only allowed for customers who opt in; otherwise we pause for manual approval.

Monitoring, dashboards and alerts:
- New Console dashboard: Standby Certification (per-region, per-model) with readiness trend, last-shadowed-request samples, and top failure modes.
- Alerts: readiness_drop (score < 60 sustained 3 runs), shadow_error_rate (>2%), mismatch_rate (>5% with recent baseline).
- Cost visibility: show incremental cost of shadowing in per-route billing breakdown.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Certification agent service in the control plane that schedules probes (Kubernetes CronJob -> initial POC), collects telemetry, and writes score to the routing policy store.
2) Traffic-shadowing module in the dataplane layer (non-blocking mirror with sampling & scrubbing).
3) Decision engine extension that consumes readiness scores and executes staged canary switchover with rollback hooks.
4) Console: UI for per-customer opt-in, certification history, and manual override.
5) QA: chaos experiments (simulate 30s region mute, KV cache eviction) and end-to-end runbook docs.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Safe scrubbing for mirrored traffic: how to deterministically remove PII for sensitive customers while preserving output quality signals? (Security/Privacy to feed in)
- Baseline generation: how frequently should we refresh the production baseline for model-output similarity?
- Operational cost cap: should we auto-throttle shadowing when spend > X% of monthly committed usage?

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives/negatives in readiness scoring -> mitigate by multi-window aggregation and human-in-the-loop for initial rollout.
- Shadowed requests leaking to observability or external systems -> ensure strict scrubbing and separate telemetry pipeline.
- Increased latency due to certification probes -> probes must be non-blocking and use low-priority execution paths.

Related artifacts and links:
- Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Standby+Certification+Spec (internal)
- Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/standby-certification-design
- Dashboard mockups: https://figma.com/file/standby-certification-mockups
- PR for initial shadowing harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6271
- Incident playbook reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Failover+Runbook

Rollout plan and timeline:
- Week 1 (POC): CronJob agent that runs probes and writes basic readiness score (no shadowing).
- Week 2: Shadowing harness + telemetry ingest into test Console.
- Week 3: Decision engine integration for internal canary routing; run chaos tests.
- Week 4: Invite a pilot customer to opt-in with manual approval gating.
- Week 6: Opt-in automatic failover for low-risk customers, GA for internal teams.

Acceptance test checklist:
- CI test that synthetic requests produce expected readiness score shape when we simulate latency or model mismatch.
- Manual e2e test: stage a canary to standby region and validate rollback triggers on injected errors.
- Security review pass for traffic scrubbing and telemetry separation.
